questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A civilized and safe city/country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very hard before I got my login to McGill's student platform, e.g. getting in touch with them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Got the key and the direction to my home

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Didn't get my address until a few days before I got there. They were kind and understanding but it would be nice to know before leaving from home.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Graduate residence sharing kitchen and bath with many other people or apartment with 2-3 roomies.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Mandatory meal plan (1300 CAD) if living in residence. Good, delicious and healthy options here but expensive. Also option to cook at home with full equipment kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's a great opportunity to meet new people from different countries and is located close to the University. It's also quite expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Different formal documents, e.g. proof of English efficiency.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much, it was hard to get in touch with them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Semi successful. You only know what courses are available for the exact term quite late, so I had to research courses several times. And it's hard to get a clear view of the classes by just reading about it, so I got a little disappointed at some point after I arrived.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
For McGill University: 
Do not study math here. 
If you want to learn French, start registration early! It requires an interview before being able to submit and there's limited spaces.
And also: check if your university makes you able to change classes within the first weeks because that makes it less stressful that you always have the opportunity to switch.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The math teaching was too loose, had one super bad lecturer (maybe I was just unlucky). I had 4th year (undergrad) and graduate courses and the level was quite low.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At McGill there was more communication between student and teacher, but it resulted in it being too easy to e.g. get an assignment postponed. In general there is also way more ongoing grading that counts towards the final grade whereas at UCPH it's usually one exam that determines your whole grade for one course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: MATH423 Applied regression, MATH682 Statistical inference, FRSL208 Near beginners French

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend the FRSL courses (French as a second language). They have a lot of good teachers at McGill and since the city is French speaking there's also good opportunity to practice you oral skills.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Didn't get my mobile service up and running immediately so I lost a lot of money on phone services the first couple of days. You also have to have your own pillow, bed sheets etc. so that was a whole bunch of new expenses since it didn't make sense to bring from home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive than expected and prices in supermarkets/restaurants in general in Canada.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
McGill has a huge gym with all sorts of fields for different sports and also their own pool. For very little money you also have access to a quite impressive fitness centre. There's even sport teams where you can join a semester long tournament on different levels.
There's a few afternoons set off for specific groups to meet, e.g. exchange students, first year's etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join an intermural sports teem

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can do (long) weekend trip to Toronto/Niagara Falls and Quebec City. There is also lots of great places to hike, both during summer and winter. Also try skiing only 30 min. outside the city. It's easy and not too expensive to rent a car (discount through McGill) for whatever activity you're doing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Montreal is the most ‘Europeanized' city in Canada so it was very easy to adapt.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the people in your classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The enormous diversity in ethnicity. There's people from all over the world and I have definitely gotten some new perspectives in meeting so many different people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go there unless you study math. 
Try to get a spot living on campus – it's a great opportunity to get friends.
As long as you pass your courses, do not hesitate to make the most of your weekends/holidays. Most people are so open and always ready to go on a trip even though you don't know each other.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would go there in the Fall term since it's insanely cold in the winter. That way you can also enjoy the beautiful campus way more.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Coming with nothing but myself and then making such good friendships and connections although we all come from very different backgrounds and don't even speak the same language. It was also a big experience being independent for so long, both study wise and just in general when trying to make an everyday life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out formalities with how to get an insurance card, booking a doctor's appointment, figuring out the online student platform etc. But it wasn't that much of a challenge.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
